summary: A field-shaped trigger that opens a calendar.

pairs.dont: Show today's date as the placeholder.
pairs.do: Say "Pick a date", and let a real value look different.
pairs.why: The only thing separating the two states is the text colour. A date-shaped placeholder reads as a value that has already been chosen.

pairs.do: Use a format with the month in words.
pairs.why: That date is in March for half the world and April for the other half, and nothing on screen says which.

pairs.dont: Make the calendar the only way in for a date far from today.
pairs.do: Pair it with a field when the range is wide.
pairs.why: A grid is the fast path for next Tuesday and the slow one for a date two years out.

pairs.dont: Close the popover as soon as the first date is clicked in range mode.
pairs.why: Half a range is not an answer, and reopening to finish it loses the context of what was already picked.

pairs.dont: Silently disable everything before a date.
pairs.do: Put the rule in the field's description.
pairs.why: People try the date they want first. If it will not take, they need to know why before they start hunting.

a11y: The trigger is a <button>, not a text input. There is no typed-date path — Enter or Space opens the calendar, which autofocuses, so focus lands where the next keystroke is expected.
The calendar icon is aria-hidden; the trigger's text is its accessible name, so an empty picker needs placeholder text that says what it selects.
In range mode the popover stays open after the first date, because a range is not a complete answer until both ends are in.
